newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ANZ's Mercer wants RBA role to be retained.
newsitem.headline: ANZ's Mercer wants RBA role to be retained.

text.p: The chief executive of Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd said on Monday that he was concerned that an industry review had recommended changes to the prudential supervisory role of the Reserve Bank.

"Not only will extra lines of communication be costly to banks, but the separation will not facilitate a fast response in times of crisis," Don Mercer said at the annual meeting of the Australian Bankers Association (ABA).

The Wallis inquiry into the financial sector recommended earlier this year that the national government establish a new prudential supervisory body which would oversee banks and other non-bank groups, removing the central bank from daily bank oversight.
However, the Reserve Bank would retain final responsibility for the health of the financial system.
Mercer said Australian bankers were also concerned that the recommended changes would remove the impression among bank depositors that their funds were safe.
On a more direct note, he also said the major banks were not colluding on the sensitive issue of mortgage rates.

"It is quite frankly preposterous to suggest that senior management of our organisations plot together to break the law. I believe that (Australian government) Ministers and senior bureaucrats know this, and the accusation was really aimed at the interest rate question -- that is, it was a political ploy rather than a geniune concern about collusion."

The most recent mortgage rate cuts by the major banks were less than the 50 basis point reduction in the official interest rate, sparking adverse comments from ministers and threats of an inquiry by the anti-monopolies body.
The ANZ, however, later added to its mortgage rate reduction, passing on the full increase.
